articulation.label: always
articulation.alt: always: /ɔ/ → /l/ → /w/ → /eɪ/ → /z/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/w/: Round the lips; raise the back of the tongue.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/z/: A narrow gap near the ridge; add voice.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Your A1 checkpoint
sections: Try the five tasks before opening the models. A partner may speak slowly or repeat. Listen to the dictation and write what you hear.
Describe two people in a family photo using he, she or they.
Say where a key, a bag and a book are. Use in, on or under.
Describe two parts of your daily routine and give a time.
Write a short message asking a person to meet you at a time and place.

Answer one new question about your home without reading a script.
Review words: always, sometimes, dream, come back, underwear. Cover the list; recall meanings and use two in your own sentences.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 060 - Review & Check - 01

segments.name: Heart
segments.text: No. Sometimes I take the bus.

cards.answer:
Dictation: No. Sometimes I take the bus.
1: For example: She is my mother. They are my grandparents.
2: For example: The key is in the bag. The book is on the table.
3: For example: I wake up at six. I leave home at eight.
4: For example: Please meet me at home at six.
5: Ask a partner to change the object or the room. Give a relevant answer, asking for repetition if needed.
For each task, note: I can do it; I can do it with repetition; I need more practice. Repeat difficult tasks another day with new details. Clear meaning matters more than a perfect accent.
